source_files.role: Ported in full. Header-only free-function library: sums, means, medians, both quantile conventions, deviations, the Tukey/winsorized/adaptive quantile family, five correlation coefficients, computeRank and SummaryStatistics.
Empty translation unit: an OpenMS namespace with no members. Hashed to record that the header carries the whole implementation and nothing was missed in a .cpp.
Ported in full. Header-only template; no .cpp exists in the SDK.
Ported in full. Header-only static templates plus three by-value free functions; no .cpp exists in the SDK.
Oracle for StatisticFunctions.h: 20 START_SECTIONs, all mapped in tests/statistic_functions.rs.

Oracle for BasicStatistics.h: 18 START_SECTIONs, all mapped in tests/basic_statistics.rs. A plain grep -c reports 20, because two further occurrences at lines 341 and 356 are inside comments that refer to a section rather than opening one. Also the origin of the 195-value dvector_data sample transcribed there.

Oracle for RankData.h: 11 START_SECTIONs, all mapped in tests/rank_data.rs. Its cross-validation section carries vectors its authors generated with SciPy 1.17.1; those are transcribed, not re-executed here.
Oracle for Histogram.h: 23 START_SECTIONs, all mapped in tests/histogram.rs. It instantiates Histogram<float, float> and mutates one shared object down the file.
Not ported. Read for the exact exception classes the four headers throw: InvalidRange, InvalidValue, OutOfRange and IndexOverflow, which the support documents map onto this crate's Error variants.
Not ported. Read for Size, SignedSize, UInt and Int, whose widths decide where the source's index arithmetic wraps.

source_anchors.operation: median averages the two middle values for an even count and returns the single middle value for an odd one, which is why it returns double rather than the element type

quantile1st takes the median of [0, size/2 - 1) for an even count; the -1 is commented as excluding the median value, but an even count has no middle element, so one real observation is dropped from the lower half
quantile3rd takes the median of [size/2 + 1, end) and drops one observation from the upper half for the same reason
quantile's sortedness precondition is OPENMS_PRECONDITION only, so it is compiled out of a release build; the port always checks and returns Error::UnsortedData
a zero fractional part short-circuits to x[idx] without touching x[idx + 1], which is what keeps q == 1 from reading past the end
tukeyUpperFence needs four finite values and a strictly positive interquartile range, and otherwise returns +infinity as the no-fence sentinel
winsorizedQuantile also caps below at 0.0, which the source's comment calls defensive for absolute residuals and which makes it unsuitable for signed data
adaptiveQuantile degenerates to a step function when r_dense <= r_sparse, rather than rejecting the configuration
variance uses std::numeric_limits<double>::max() as the sentinel for an unsupplied mean, so a caller that means DBL_MAX cannot say so; the port splits the overload instead

variance divides by distance - 1 unchecked and returns NaN for a single value; covariance at line 624 does the same; meanSquareError at line 658 divides by n instead, and these different degrees of freedom are preserved exactly
covariance re-tests the two begin iterators inside its loop, a loop-invariant check, so a shorter second range is dereferenced out of bounds before the trailing checkIteratorsEqual notices
matthewsCorrelationCoefficient calls checkIteratorsNotNULL(begin_a, end_b), comparing iterators from two different containers, which is undefined behaviour and not the emptiness check it intends

pearsonCorrelationCoefficient returns numerator / sqrt(denominator_a * denominator_b); a constant range zeroes a denominator and the documented result is NaN, which the port returns explicitly after proving the numerator is zero in that case
computeRank computes Size n = w.size() - 1 in unsigned arithmetic, which wraps to SIZE_MAX for an empty vector

computeRank detects ties with the relative test |a - b| > 1e-7 * |later|, so the tolerance collapses to zero next to a zero and a chain of near-neighbours becomes one block; the tie rank is 0.5 * (i + z + 1)
rankCorrelationCoefficient correlates about the theoretical mean rank (n + 1) / 2 rather than the observed mean of the ranks, with a comment recording the earlier integer division
rankCorrelationCoefficient returns 0 when either sum of squares is zero, where pearsonCorrelationCoefficient returns NaN for the same situation
SummaryStatistics substitutes 0.0 for the variance when count <= 1, acknowledging in a comment that the n-1 divisor is undefined there
update repairs a zero probability mass by zeroing mean and variance after the division; the coordinate overload at line 113 has no such guard and leaves both NaN
the coordinate overload takes only a coordinate begin iterator and advances it once per probability, reading past the end of a shorter coordinate range
normalDensity_sqrt2pi is exp of the standardised square with no 1/sqrt(variance) scaling, so it is exactly 1 at the mean for every variance; it divides by the variance unchecked
sqrt2pi() is the literal 2.50662827463100050240, which parses to the f64 2.5066282746310007, one ulp above the correctly rounded sqrt(2 pi) 2.5066282746310002; the port keeps the source value
normalApproximationHelper_ divides each density by the summed density and multiplies by sum(), in that order, so the output carries the distribution's own mass; the divisor is not checked
nan_policy Propagate returns an all-NaN vector as soon as any NaN is present, for every tie method, matching SciPy
indices are stable-sorted by the values promoted to double using <, under which -0.0 and 0.0 are equal; the port uses partial_cmp rather than the IEEE-754 total order so Ordinal keeps that behaviour
tie blocks are found by exact equality of the promoted values, unlike computeRank's relative tolerance; the one-based ranks of a block spanning [lo, hi) are lo+1 through hi
rightBorderOfBin returns nextafter(maxBound(), maxBound() + 1) for the last bin, because valueToBin routes max into it regardless of the bin arithmetic
maxValue and minValue dereference max_element/min_element over bins_ without checking that it is non-empty, which a default-constructed histogram is
reset clears bins_ and assigns the new bounds before throwing on a non-positive bin size, leaving a half-updated object; the port builds the new bins first
applyLogTransformation casts multiplier * log(x + 1) back to ValueType, so the default UInt instantiation truncates to an integer, and it does not check the sign of the logarithm's argument
valueToBin's two bound comparisons are both false for a NaN, which then reaches floor(NaN) and a conversion to the unsigned Size
initBins_ computes Size(ceil((max_ - min_) / bin_size_)) with no check that max_ >= min_ and no ceiling on the result; max_ == min_ is special-cased to a single bin

evidence.description: Tier 3 is the transcription of every literal in the four class tests, section by section, with the source line recorded above each Rust test. Tier 4 covers the expectations derived independently from a closed form, a symmetry or an invariant, and the Rust-only guards. No retained C++ output and no oracle driver exists for these headers, so no tier 1 or tier 2 claim is made for the free functions themselves. The SORTING behaviour is the exception and has tier 1 evidence at one remove, through two consumers: ../oracle/ffap-complete-fix1 and ../oracle/ffap-instr-completion validate crate::math::source_sort itself against libstdc++ over 2,272 inputs carrying ties, signed zeros, infinities and four NaN bit patterns, and ../oracle/a7-fileinfo's five frozen -s reports (c_nan_one_s, c_nan_two_s, c_nan_then_finite_s, c_finite_then_nan_s, c_zero_swapped_s) are what tests/file_info_a7.rs compares these functions' output against, line for line, since the shared-math wave.

sections.grep_count_note: A plain grep -c START_SECTION over the four files reports 74. Two of those occurrences are inside comments in BasicStatistics_test.cpp at lines 341 and 356 and open no section, so the real total is 72 and all 72 are mapped.

independently_derived: MeanAbsoluteDeviation of the seven-value z_odd sample is exactly 6/7, against the class test's truncated 0.857142
MeanAbsoluteDeviation of {-1,0,1,2,3} about 1 is exactly 6/5, which is representable, so the test asserts equality rather than a tolerance
MAD of {-1,0,1,2,3,4} is 1.5 for both the median the class test's `true` literal supplies (1.0) and the median its comment states (1.5)
Spearman correlation of a strictly increasing sequence with itself is exactly +1 and with its reversal exactly -1, by the symmetry of the ranks about mu
computeRank's tie block for four equal values starting at sorted position 3 gets 0.5*(3+7+1) = 5.5, the mean of ranks 4..7

adaptive quantile case A: Q1 = 2 and Q3 = 7 over the sorted base give a Tukey fence of 14.5, a tail fraction of exactly 1/201, a raw quantile of 0.6*9 + 0.4*1000 and a robust quantile of 0.6*9 + 0.4*14.5

a zero denominator in the Matthews and Pearson coefficients forces a zero numerator in every reachable case, so the source's unchecked division yields NaN and the explicit NaN is an equivalence rather than a substitution
BasicStatistics weighted mean and variance of {0,1,3,2,0} are exactly 13/6 and 17/36
BasicStatistics coordinates 1000 - i reflect the positions, so the weighted mean reflects: mean == 1000 - mean(positions)
the normal approximation's entries sum to sum(), because each is density/total_density * sum
the source's sqrt2pi literal is exactly one ulp above sqrt(2 pi), asserted on the bit patterns
rankdata Average is the exact midpoint of Min and Max at every position, and Ordinal is a permutation of 1..=n
Histogram bin counts 10, 5 and 6 follow from ceil((max - min) / bin_size)
the log-transformed last histogram bin is exactly ln(10001), against the class test's rounded 9.21044

the libstdc++ permutation itself: every expected array in the_sorting_entry_points_reproduce_the_release_builds_permutation, the_introsort_threshold_decides_where_a_nan_lands and a_signed_zero_keeps_the_order_the_release_build_keeps is derived from __insertion_sort's two branches, __move_median_to_first's swap and _S_threshold == 16, not from this crate's output -- and the three NaN positions they pin (index 0, 8 and 10 for {NaN, 2..16}, {NaN, 2..17} and {NaN, 2..20}) are the ones measured against the reference compiler, so derivation and measurement agree

the NaN bit patterns of a_generated_nan_carries_the_release_builds_bits follow from the SSE2 rules of Intel SDM vol. 1 (first NaN operand quieted, or the real-indefinite QNaN 0xfff8000000000000 for an invalid operation, and andpd clearing the sign bit) applied to the instruction the Release build emits

the invariant the x86_64 helpers rest on -- that they are the identity on every non-NaN result, so no finite value can move -- which the_x86_64_helpers_change_no_finite_result asserts bit for bit against the plain-Rust arithmetic rather than against a frozen literal

native_boundaries: statistic_functions: MAX_ITEMS = 50,000,000 values and MAX_BYTES = 512 MiB per staged buffer, checked with checked_mul in a preflight before any allocation, for mad, tukey_upper_fence, winsorized_quantile, adaptive_quantile, compute_rank and rank_correlation_coefficient
basic_statistics: MAX_ITEMS = 50,000,000 probabilities, coordinates or approximation points, checked before the state is cleared
rank_data: MAX_ITEMS = 50,000,000 values, checked before either staging buffer is allocated
histogram: MAX_BINS = 16,777,216 bins, checked against the caller-controlled ceil((max - min) / bin_size) before the vector is allocated
Sortedness is always verified where the source states it only as a precondition, including for a one-element range, which std::is_sorted accepts even when that element is NaN

statistic_functions: since the shared-math wave of 2026-09-19 and lead decision D16, every entry point that ORDERS values reproduces the permutation the Linux x86_64 Release build's std::sort leaves rather than refusing a NaN. sort_ascending is source_sort_by(&mut values, |a, b| a < b) -- std::sort(begin, end) with the default operator<, the call at MATH/StatisticFunctions.h:140 (median), :244 (quantile1st), :281 (quantile3rd), :189 (MAD, through its own median) and :948 (SummaryStatistics's unqualified sort) at pin bc9cc12 -- reproduced comparison by comparison and move by move by crate::math::source_sort from the GCC 14.4.0 libstdc++ headers the reference build was compiled with. median, quantile1st, quantile3rd, mad and SummaryStatistics::new therefore summarise a NaN-bearing sample; SummaryStatistics::of_nan_sample and the two-shape special case it existed for are gone, and SummaryStatistics::new reads its order statistics through the private _of_sorted helpers because std::sort's own output is not ascending when a NaN is in it. THREE refusals remain, each for its own reason. (1) The D1 one, inside source_sort: InvalidValue at exactly the step where the introsort's unbounded partition or final-insertion loop would read outside the vector, which is undefined behaviour with no reproducible result; only a comparison that is not asymmetric can provoke it, and < on f64 keys is asymmetric with NaN keys too, so no NaN input is turned away in practice. (2) median_sorted, quantile1st_sorted, quantile3rd_sorted and quantile return UnsortedData, because they do not sort -- they verify a CALLER's claim to have sorted, which a NaN makes false. (3) compute_rank and rank_correlation_coefficient return InvalidValue: their std::sort (:829-830) is a lambda comparing std::pair::second rather than the default operator<, and a NaN additionally defeats their relative tie test, whose two comparisons are both false against a NaN and which would therefore merge every block the NaN touches -- a second, independent behaviour that no oracle row measures. For a NaN-free range the two sorts agree on the ranks anyway, because operator< and total_cmp differ only on +-0.0, which the tie test makes one block either way. Where the NaN lands is the libstdc++ algorithm's answer and is pinned: __introsort_loop runs only while the range is longer than _S_threshold, enumerated as 16 (stl_algo.h:1806, :1880, :1899-1910), so {NaN, 2..16} keeps the NaN at index 0, {NaN, 2..17} moves it to index 8 and {NaN, 2..20} to index 10 -- which is why that sample prints minimum: 2 and median: -nan -- and even below the threshold a block move can carry it, as {3, NaN, 2} sorting to {2, 3, NaN} shows. the_introsort_threshold_decides_where_a_nan_lands pins the whole permutation for all three sizes, and the_sorting_entry_points_reproduce_the_release_builds_permutation the rest. The SAME std::sort equivalence without a NaN is reproduced by the same change: -0.0 and 0.0 are equivalent under operator<, std::sort's precondition holds, libstdc++ leaves them in input order, and so does sort_ascending now -- where it used to order them by f64::total_cmp, which puts -0.0 first. That closes native difference 6 of docs/FILE_INFO_A7_SUPPORT.md, measured in both orders (oracle cases c_nan_one_s and c_zero_swapped_s) and now pinned as an EQUALITY by consensus_a_signed_zero_sample_keeps_the_release_builds_order and by a_signed_zero_keeps_the_order_the_release_build_keeps. mad no longer refuses a NaN median or a NaN difference manufactured by inf - inf: the source stages the same differences and hands them to the same std::sort. Infinities are ordered, not refused. CPP-347 is rewritten as closed-by-reproduction; the C++ defect -- order statistics read positionally out of a range whose order the comparison did not determine -- stands.
variance, sd and covariance refuse n < 2 instead of dividing by zero; SummaryStatistics keeps the source's 0.0 for n <= 1
Every division by a caller-influenced denominator is either checked or replaced by the value the division would have produced, with the equivalence stated at the item

Histogram refuses an inverted range, a non-finite bound, width, value or increment, a NaN lookup, and a bin at or below -1 in the log transformation; reset and apply_log_transformation commit atomically
BasicStatistics::update_with_coordinates compares the two lengths instead of walking an unbounded coordinate iterator
compute_rank on an empty slice is a no-op rather than an unsigned wrap

BasicStatistics::normal_approximation(0) and normal_approximation_at(&[]) succeed and return empty, because normalApproximationHelper_ runs both of its loops zero times and never divides by gaussSum; the zero-sum refusal applies only where the source would actually divide

statistic_functions: a NaN this module GENERATES out of non-NaN operands carries the Linux x86_64 Release build's bits on every host, not the host's. IEEE 754 fixes every finite result of + - * / sqrt but not which NaN an invalid operation yields; SSE2 yields the real-indefinite QNaN 0xfff8000000000000 (which glibc spells -nan) and an arm64 host yields 0x7ff8000000000000. Every function here whose own arithmetic can generate one is built on crate::math::x86_64: sum, mean, variance, variance_with_mean, sd, sd_with_mean, covariance, mean_square_error, root_mean_square_error, mean_absolute_deviation, mad's fabs, median_of_sorted's even-size average and quantile's linear blend. Not rebuilt, and why: classification_rate and matthews_correlation_coefficient count with comparisons, compute_rank averages small integers, and tukey_upper_fence, tail_fraction_above, winsorized_quantile and adaptive_quantile drop every non-finite value first as the source's std::isfinite filter does, so none of them can generate a NaN. pearson_correlation_coefficient and matthews_correlation_coefficient are a known gap rather than an argument: both substitute an explicit f64::NAN for a division the source performs, a divergence that predates this wave, so making only their other operations bit-faithful would leave that substituted NaN as the single host-shaped value; the crate's bit-faithful Pearson is analysis::feature_finder_picked::scoring::source_pearson and converging the two needs an oracle row. The helpers return the IEEE result whenever it is not a NaN, so no finite value changes -- asserted bit for bit by the_x86_64_helpers_change_no_finite_result against the plain-Rust arithmetic the module used before, over a battery reaching subnormals, both zeros, DBL_MAX and ranges whose squared deviations overflow. No frozen expectation moved. TWO OPERAND ORDERS ARE NOT MEASURED and are recorded as such rather than glossed: SSE2's two-operand instructions return the DESTINATION operand quieted when both operands are NaN, so where the source writes a commutative operation on two distinct temporaries, which one GCC leaves in the destination register decides the payload -- a register-allocation fact the source does not fix. covariance multiplies (*iter_a - mean_a) * (*iter_b - mean_b) at StatisticFunctions.h:619, reachable with a[i] a payload NaN while b[i] == mean_b == +inf, and the port answers with the a-derived NaN's payload. median_of_sorted's even-size case adds (*(it + n/2 - 1) + *(it + n/2)), reachable since D16 through median(&mut [nan_a, nan_b]) with two distinct payloads, and the port answers with nan_a's. No oracle row measures either and none was invented; one call each on exactly those inputs on the Linux x86_64 Release build with the result read back as bits, or a disassembly of the two loops in the reference libOpenMS.so, would settle them. Everywhere else the order is forced: subsd and divsd are not commutative, mul(diff, diff) has one operand twice, an accumulating sum += x makes the accumulator the destination, and quantile's blend refuses a NaN range. a_generated_nan_carries_the_release_builds_bits pins fifteen bit patterns derived from the SSE2 rules of Intel SDM vol. 1 rather than from this crate's output, including the POSITIVE NaN andpd leaves behind in mean_absolute_deviation and the quieted payload a signalling NaN input keeps. One shape reads the other way round and is pinned as such: variance_with_mean(&[+inf, -inf], 0.0) generates no NaN at all -- both squared deviations are +inf and they add, so the result is +inf. The indefinite NaN appears where a SUBTRACTION cancels two infinities: variance(&[1.0, +inf]), which is the FileInfo path, and variance_with_mean(&[+inf, -inf], +inf). The SPELLING is a separate layer and is not decided here: format::file_info::text_format writes every NaN as nan where glibc writes -nan for one whose sign bit is set (native difference 5 of docs/FILE_INFO_SUPPORT.md). That file was deliberately not touched, and it also needs A2's oracle row re-captured against the Linux Release build.
openmp: None of the four headers carries a #pragma omp, so there is no parallel behaviour to match and no performance gap to record for this group.
